$comment: A Go service. Shows that the harness does not care about the stack — only that every claim reduces to an exit code. Note there is no `setup`: Go modules are cached per-machine, not per-worktree, so a fresh worktree needs nothing. That is the one thing to check when porting: what does a tree containing ONLY tracked files lack?

anchors.$comment: gofmt -l prints unformatted files and still exits 0. Wrapping it in `test -z` is what turns it into an anchor — a check that cannot fail is not a check.

lanes.why: forward-only numbering — two agents cannot both mint the next migration number
regenerating protobuf stubs rewrites a shared generated tree; two agents regenerating from different .proto states produce a merge nothing can reconcile

pairedArtifacts.help: Every forward migration ships its rollback. If the change is genuinely irreversible (a DROP of data), waive it by name and say why — an irreversible migration should be a decision someone signed, not a missing file.
